definitions.gloss: setting up a meal; laying out dishes
definitions.explanation: The original meaning: preparing and arranging dishes and utensils for a meal.

definitions.gloss: preparation; arrangement; setting things up for someone
definitions.explanation: By extension, preparing or arranging things in advance so that something will go smoothly. Often implies doing the groundwork so that someone else can proceed easily.

examples.english: To prepare the table / to set things up.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}が{来|く}る{前|まえ}に{膳立|ぜんだ}てをしておいた。
examples.english: I set up the table before the guests arrived.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}が{全部|ぜんぶ}{膳立|ぜんだ}てしてくれたので、{料理|りょうり}はすぐに{始|はじ}められた。
examples.english: My mother set everything up for me, so I could start cooking right away.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}が{膳立|ぜんだ}てしてくれた。
examples.english: My boss set things up for me.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{膳立|ぜんだ}てが{整|ととの}った。
examples.english: The preparations for the meeting are in order.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のために{転職|てんしょく}の{膳立|ぜんだ}てをしたのに、{結局|けっきょく}{断|ことわ}られた。
examples.english: I arranged everything for his job change, but in the end he turned it down.

notes:
Compound of {膳|ぜん} (dining tray/table) and {立|た}て (setting up). Originally referred to laying out a meal, but now commonly used figuratively to mean preparing or arranging things in advance for someone.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {膳立|ぜんだ}てをする: to make preparations, to set things up
- {膳立|ぜんだ}てが{整|ととの}う: preparations are in order
- {膳立|ぜんだ}てが{出来|でき}ている: everything is set up and ready

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {準備|じゅんび}: preparation — the most general and common word for getting ready
- {段取|だんど}り: arrangement, planning — focuses on the order and logistics of preparation
- {手配|てはい}: arrangement — arranging for people or resources, often in a business context
- {下準備|したじゅんび}: preliminary preparation — basic prep work done in advance
